start_here: Say to your AI: "Run the Namespace files server in dav mode so I can open my files in Finder", with {"mode":"dav","state_folder":"/home/example/namespace-state"}. It runs tool:run-the-namespace-files-server on your computer and your files appear at http://127.0.0.1:38481/ until it is stopped.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it serves your files from your own store and keeps its names in a state folder, not in a list.
instructions: 1. Make sure your files-store connection (your S3-compatible store: secret, key id, bucket, endpoint, region) is saved in your vault, and pick an empty folder in your home for the state, for example /home/example/namespace-state. Your names are kept as rows in a SQLite file there unless settings.json `store` names your Postgres database (its connection string, own-rows-postgres-connection, attached as a field).

2. Say to your AI: "Run the Namespace files server in dav mode", with {"mode":"dav","state_folder":"/home/example/namespace-state"}. The AI runs tool:run-the-namespace-files-server at @workshop-tools with method tools:run; the first run builds the program and makes the names file from your connection.

3. In Finder choose Go, Connect to Server and enter http://127.0.0.1:38481/ . To give an AI the same files as tools, run the same tool with {"mode":"mcp","state_folder":"/home/example/namespace-state"} as its stdio MCP server.

4. To share a file, give the run your records door (settings.json `share`) and say to your AI: "Share /Notes/a.txt for a day". The run's share_file signs one link for the file's object, keeps it in a namespace-shared-file record of yours and runs tool:share-anything to share that record with a link; stop the share with tool:share-anything (op stop) and the next reader is refused.

worked_examples.title: Open my files in Finder
worked_examples.ask: Run the Namespace files server in dav mode so I can open my files in Finder
worked_examples.given: The input {"mode":"dav","state_folder":"/home/example/namespace-state"} and a saved files-store connection.
worked_examples.hands_back: Nothing is printed; the WebDAV folder answers on 127.0.0.1 port 38481, so Finder connects to http://127.0.0.1:38481/ and lists your names.

worked_examples.title: Give an AI my files as tools
worked_examples.ask: Run the Namespace files server over stdio for my AI
worked_examples.given: The input {"mode":"mcp","state_folder":"/home/example/namespace-state"} and a saved files-store connection.
worked_examples.hands_back: The program answers JSON-RPC lines on stdout: tools/list names "list_files", "read_file_span", "write_file", "move_names" and the rest.
